request: Source ticket: MAG-69 — 6. Re-key analytics.vehicle_metrics and vehicle_metric_watermarks on tesla_id. Step 6 of MAG-63. One migration on both tables: collapse duplicate (tesla_id, metric_date) rows, replace vehicle_metrics_account_tesla_date_unique with UNIQUE (tesla_id, metric_date), replace idx_vehicle_metrics_latest with (tesla_id, metric_date DESC), replace vehicle_metric_watermarks_account_tesla_source_unique with UNIQUE (tesla_id, source), DROP COLUMN account_id from both. Drop account_id from the queries and accountID from the Reader/Recalculator ports. LatestMetricsByAccount becomes LatestMetricsForVehicles. Unit tests: excluded. MAG-71 was cancelled and its work folds in here.

review.brief: Review tier 1 of RM59 (change RM59-analytics-rekey-vehicle-metrics-on-tesla-id, ticket MAG-69). Read the diff from f24ab446237c99a3508a84cb2ee77cb1a0d938dc to HEAD, not the whole module. Validate: (1) the migration matches the user-confirmed design in design.md exactly - a mismatch on any schema object is a blocker finding; (2) every query in query.sql lost account_id and LatestVehicleMetricsByVehicles filters on tesla_id = ANY; (3) the five port signatures in analytics.go match design.md D9/D10, and LatestMetricsForVehicles takes []vehicleref.Ref; (4) module boundaries - internal/analytics imports no other module's db package, and the leader-owned edits in internal/app and internal/gateway go through public interfaces only; (5) the existing tests were fixed, not weakened - no test deleted, no assertion removed to make a failure go away, and the renamed tests still assert the same behaviour; (6) the read-heavy Performance-Profile - the index plan still serves the latest-row query with no Sort node; (7) doc comments carry no change-doc citation (no design.md, no D-ids, no RM/CH ids, no tier or wave numbers) per the B2 comment rule; (8) the docs-track-change rule - AGENTS.md, README.md, ai/architecture.md and kkpa/context/ no longer name the old port. KNOWN AND EXPECTED, not findings: go vet ./internal/gateway/... is red (three gateway test files are tier 2's job, design.md D12); openspec/specs/gateway/spec.md still names the old port (tier 2 owns that delta); openspec/specs/analytics/spec.md's Module-Scoped Database Schema requirement is deliberately unchanged (tasks.md 7.3); historic migrations and kkpa/context/pending-spec-to-sync/applied/ snapshots are never edited. SIGNAL PROVENANCE: go build, go vet, gofmt and the four guards were run by the ASSISTANT. The test suite (go test ./internal/analytics/... ./internal/app/...) was run and reported passing by the OWNER. You do NOT run the suite - judge test quality by reading the tests.

findings.note: internal/analytics/db_integration_test.go:181,2305,2307,2564,2641 — comment lines this change edited (function renames, LatestMetricsByAccount to LatestMetricsForVehicles) still cite change-doc identifiers left over from the rename: 'task 6.4(b)' (181), 'Task 5.3' (2305), 'RM38-A/RM38-C' (2307), 'task 2.5' (2564), 'design.md's Test Contract ... (task' (2641). The B2 comment rule treats an edited line that keeps such a citation as a finding, and the same edit already shows the cleanup done correctly elsewhere in this file (fetchWatermark's comment dropped its 'Index Plan #4' citation). Fix by writing the reason in place of the citation, same as that one. | LEADER: accepted and fixed. Eight comment spots rewritten to state the reason instead of the citation. go vet and gofmt still clean.

internal/gateway/handlers/external_charges.go:720 — 'if refs, _, ok := h.ownedVehicles(ctx, uid); teslaIDFilter != 0 && ...' calls h.ownedVehicles, which re-reads h.acct.RegisteredVehicles, even though buildExternalChargesPage already fetched the same account's vehicles at line 665 into `vehicles`. This is a second DB read on a read-heavy hot path. It matches design.md D12's explicit instruction (guard-compliance forces going through ownedVehicles rather than reusing the local slice), so this is not a design deviation — flagging it for tier 2's full gateway-authorization rewrite (RM59-gateway-authorize-metrics-reads) to fix, not a blocker here. | LEADER: accepted as correct, deferred to tier 2 on the reviewer's own reasoning - D12 forces the ownedVehicles call here, and tier 2 rewrites this function. Recorded in tier 2's roadmap row so the dispatch cannot lose it. Not fixed in tier 1.
